issues.justification: A high Timeout value of 300 seconds allows attackers to initiate many connections and keep them open for a long time, consuming server resources and making the service less responsive. This leads to gradual resource exhaustion but does not cause an immediate crash.
issues.recommendation: Set 'Timeout 10' or shorter in the Apache configuration.

issues.justification: Enabling the autoindex module allows directory listings, revealing file and directory names which can aid attackers in understanding the server's structure and identifying potential vulnerabilities.
issues.recommendation: Comment out or remove the 'LoadModule autoindex_module modules/mod_autoindex.so' directive from httpd.conf to disable the mod_autoindex module.

issues.justification: Enabling mod_status provides detailed server performance statistics, which can be used by attackers to refine their attacks based on the current load and configuration of the server.
issues.recommendation: Comment out or remove the 'LoadModule status_module modules/mod_status.so' directive in httpd.conf.

issues.recommendation: Set 'Options None' or 'Options Multiviews' in the web root <Directory> directive.

issues.justification: ServerTokens OS exposes the operating system version in every HTTP response header, enabling attackers to precisely target known CVEs for the disclosed OS.
issues.recommendation: Set 'ServerTokens Prod' to expose only the product name.

issues.justification: ServerSignature On discloses the Apache version and server name in error pages, allowing attackers to target known vulnerabilities specific to that version.
issues.recommendation: Set 'ServerSignature Off' to remove the signature from server-generated documents.

issues.justification: Without a Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options header, Apache does not prevent clickjacking attacks where an attacker frames the site inside an iframe on a malicious page. UI redressing can trick users into performing unintended actions on the legitimate site.
issues.recommendation: Add 'Header always append Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self'"' to the server configuration.

issues.recommendation: Add 'Header set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"' to the server configuration.

chains.justification: AllowOverride All lets a user-controlled .htaccess override server configuration, and Options FollowSymLinks/Indexes widens what that config can reach — enabling symlink-based path traversal and directory listing. Whether this reaches code execution depends on which handlers the .htaccess is allowed to enable, so it is a strong path-exposure and config-override risk rather than guaranteed RCE.
Permissive Timeout + KeepAliveTimeout + unbounded MaxKeepAliveRequests create compounding resource exhaustion vectors. An attacker can hold connections open and multiply the DoS impact.
Both ServerTokens and ServerSignature leaking version details compound the information disclosure risk, giving attackers precise version targeting.
Enabling the status module with LoadModule and setting ServerTokens to Full reveals detailed server information, aiding attackers in reconnaissance and targeted exploitation.

The status_module exposes runtime internals via /server-status, and Apache running as root means any process compromise inherits root. Combined, reconnaissance is easier and the blast radius of any other flaw is maximal — running as a non-root user would contain that impact. This chain raises exposure and severity of a separate flaw rather than granting escalation on its own.

Enabling Options All and loading the status_module allows an attacker to access detailed server statistics via /server-status, which can be used for further reconnaissance or denial of service attacks.
Enabling Options Indexes and loading the autoindex_module allows directory listings to be displayed, which can expose sensitive file structures and facilitate further reconnaissance or exploitation.
WebDAV modules (dav_module, dav_fs_module) loaded with permissive AllowOverride enables remote file upload and execution. This chain has the highest amplification — remote code execution in one step.
